description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percent) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and IKE—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents ACC (%) on a linear scale, ranging from 60% to 80%. The 'Base' method is shown as a solid black line with circular markers, starting at approximately 62.5% and increasing to about 68.5%. The 'MEND' method is depicted as a brown dashed line with diamond markers, beginning at roughly 69% and rising to about 77%. The 'FT' method is a blue dashed line with triangular markers, starting near 64% and ending at approximately 70.5%. The 'MEMIT' method is represented by a purple dashed line with circular markers, beginning at around 68% and increasing to about 75%. The 'IKE' method is shown as a red dashed line with triangular markers, starting at approximately 66% and rising to about 72%. The 'MEND' line consistently achieves the highest accuracy across the entire range of co-occurrence numbers, while the 'Base' line consistently achieves the lowest accuracy.
